raw_text:
Goal: one-week deload (Week 5) for an advanced 26-year-old male after 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy (≈18 working sets/session, compounds at ~RPE 8.5). Use the same exercises but reduce volume and intensity. Keep movement patterns to maintain technique and neural priming, promote recovery, and prevent detraining. Full-gym access is assumed.

Deload principles applied:
- Reduce volume to ~30–50% of normal working sets (target ~6–9 working sets per session).
- Reduce intensity to ~60–70% of usual intensity or target RPE 5–6 on main compound sets.
- Keep tempo normal, avoid training to failure, keep reps technically clean.
- Maintain frequency (same number of sessions as usual, unless you want to reduce frequency — here we keep 4 sessions as typical for advanced hypertrophy split; if the client previously trained 4–6x/week, pick the lower end). I’ll present a 4-session week (e.g., Upper/Lower split ×2).
- Keep accessory movements but drastically cut sets and avoid heavy single-leg or heavy CNS-taxing lifts.
- Add mobility, soft-tissue work, and optional low-intensity cardio for recovery.
- Sleep, protein, and calorie guidance: maintain protein, slightly reduce calories only if weight loss is desired; otherwise keep calories near maintenance. Prioritize sleep and hydration.

Weekly structure (4 sessions): Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B. Session order spaced with at least one rest/recovery day midweek or after two sessions — example: Mon (Upper A), Tue (Lower A), Thu (Upper B), Sat (Lower B). Include optional active recovery on Wed and Sun.

Session format guidelines:
- Warm-up: 8–12 minutes light aerobic (bike/row), dynamic mobility for target joints, and 2–3 warm-up sets for main compound (light).
- Working sets: keep compounds 2–3 working sets at RPE 5–6, accessories 1–2 sets at RPE 5–6.
- Rest intervals: slightly shorter than heavy weeks — 60–120s for compounds, 45–90s for accessories.
- Tempo: controlled (2s eccentric, 1s pause optional, 1s concentric), avoid ballistic effort.
- Avoid heavy singles, heavy negatives, or metabolic finishers.

Example deload week (use same exercises your client has been doing; I’ll use typical exercises for hypertrophy blocks — substitute exact variations your client used):

Day 1 — Upper A (Mon)
Warm-up: 8–10 min easy row/bike + shoulder/thoracic mobility, band pull-aparts
1) Barbell Bench Press (same variation used previously) — 3 sets × 6–8 reps @ ~60–70% or RPE 5–6
2) Bent-over Barbell Row (or chest-supported row if that was used) — 3 sets × 6–8 reps @ RPE 5–6
3) Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press — 2 sets × 8–10 reps @ RPE 5–6
4) Wide-grip Lat Pulldown (or pull-up variation) — 2 sets × 8–10 reps @ RPE 5–6
5) Incline Dumbbell Fly or Cable Fly — 1–2 sets × 10–12 reps, light, focus on tempo
6) Face pulls or banded external rotations — 2 sets × 12–15 reps, mobility-focused

Optional: 10–20 minutes low-intensity cardio (walk, bike) or mobility/foam rolling

Day 2 — Lower A (Tue)
Warm-up: 8–10 min bike + hip mobility, ankle drills, bodyweight squats
1) Back Squat (same variation used) — 3 sets × 5–7 reps @ ~60–70% or RPE 5–6
2) Romanian Deadlift (or hinge variation used) — 2 sets × 6–8 reps @ RPE 5–6
3) Bulgarian Split Squat (bodyweight or light dumbbells) — 2 sets × 8–10 reps per leg, controlled
4) Leg Press or Hack Squat (if previously used) — 1–2 sets × 10–12 reps, light
5) Standing Calf Raise — 2 sets × 10–15 reps, controlled
6) Core: Pallof press or dead bug — 2 sets × 10–12 each side, focus on control

Optional: 10–20 min walk or easy bike after session

Day 3 — Active recovery or rest (Wed)
Option: 20–40 minutes low-intensity cardio (walking, easy swim, bike), mobility, soft tissue work, stretching. Keep heart rate low; no strength work.

Day 4 — Upper B (Thu)
Warm-up: 8–10 min row + rotator cuff warm-up
1) Overhead Press (barbell or variation previously used) — 2–3 sets × 5–7 reps @ RPE 5–6
2) Incline Barbell or Dumbbell Press — 2 sets × 6–8 reps @ RPE 5–6
3) Single-arm Dumbbell Row or Chest-supported Row — 2 sets × 8–10 reps each arm @ RPE 5–6
4) Cable Lateral Raise — 1–2 sets × 10–12 reps, light
5) Hammer Curl or EZ-bar Curl — 1–2 sets × 10–12 reps
6) Triceps Rope Pushdown or Overhead Triceps Extension — 1–2 sets × 10–12 reps

Optional: 10–15 minutes mobility / thoracic extension work

Day 5 — Lower B (Sat)
Warm-up: 8–10 min bike + hip hinge patterning, glute activation
1) Deadlift (same variation used; if conventional used, keep lighter, or switch to trap bar for less CNS stress) — 2 sets × 4–6 reps @ RPE 5–6
2) Front Squat or Goblet Squat (if front was used previously; pick the same) — 2 sets × 6–8 reps @ RPE 5–6
3) Glute Bridge / Hip Thrust (light) — 2 sets × 8–10 reps
4) Single-leg Romanian Deadlift or Good Morning (light) — 1–2 sets × 8–10 reps per leg
5) Seated Calf or Standing Calf — 2 sets × 12–15 reps
6) Core: Plank variations — 2 × 45–60s or 3 × 30–45s with good form

Day 6 — Light activity or rest (Sun)
Active recovery: easy walk, recreational mobility work, foam rolling. Focus on sleep and nutrition.

General intensity notes:
- Use roughly 60–70% of normal working loads or pick a weight that lands around RPE 5–6. If you typically did sets at RPE 8–9 for compounds, reduce by ~2.5–3 RPE (stop well short of failure).
- Keep total working sets per session near 6–9. Accessories should be 1–2 sets each.
- If the client usually trains 5–6 days and wants to reduce frequency, you can compress to 3 full-body/upper-lower sessions; the key is the same reduction in volume/intensity.

Nutrition and recovery guidance for the deload week:
- Protein: maintain usual intake (2.0–2.4 g/kg LBM if aiming to preserve muscle; at minimum 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight). Don’t drop protein just because training volume is lower.
- Calories: slight reduction (≈100–300 kcal/day) is optional if the client is not aiming to gain and wants to avoid small weight gain from reduced activity. If the client is preparing for a subsequent block and wants to maximize performance, keeping calories at maintenance is fine.
- Carbs: keep moderate around training to support performance and recovery.
- Hydration: maintain or slightly increase water intake.
- Sleep: prioritize 8+ hours when possible to maximize neural recovery.
- Active recovery: foam rolling, mobility work, light aerobic sessions to promote blood flow and recovery.

Monitoring/notes:
- Rate of perceived recovery and readiness can guide daily adjustments. If the client still feels fatigued, reduce session count (drop one session) or reduce sets further.
- Avoid adding conditioning that spikes HR >70% HRmax for long periods; keep cardio easy.
- Use this week to address any niggles: include targeted mobility, soft tissue, and corrective exercises.
- Keep technical work on compounds — use light sets to groove movement patterns.

Example daily loads (if you want concrete percentages): for compound lifts use 60–70% 1RM for 2–3 sets of 4–8 reps (or choose a weight that feels like RPE 5–6). Accessories at 50–60% of usual training weights for 1–2 sets.

If you want this formatted into a printable one-page cheat sheet with the exact exercises your client used in the prior block substituted in, tell me those exact exercises and I’ll tailor sets/reps and sequencing to match them precisely.
